advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that calls run_http_with_grace with uvicorn_graceful_seconds=<v> and asserts timeout_graceful_shutdown == int(v), overriding the default backstop.
evidence: src/rebar/_mcp_serving.py:137-138: `if uvicorn_graceful_seconds is not None: uvicorn_backstop_seconds = uvicorn_graceful_seconds`
Search of tests/ for `uvicorn_graceful_seconds` returns (no matches) — the compat override path has zero coverage.

Named violating input: `run_http_with_grace(server, gauge, uvicorn_graceful_seconds=5)` should produce captured timeout_graceful_shutdown == 5; a regression dropping the override would pass all existing tests, since the transport test at test_mcp_http_transport.py:529 only passes grace_seconds and asserts the default 30.
advisory.finding: The newly added `uvicorn_graceful_seconds` backward-compatibility keyword override in run_http_with_grace is never exercised by any test; passing `uvicorn_graceful_seconds=<value>` must override `uvicorn_backstop_seconds` and reach `timeout_graceful_shutdown=int(...)`, but no test drives this path.
scenarios: A refactor removes or mis-wires the compat override; existing tests stay green while callers using the old keyword silently get the wrong backstop.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a transport test mirroring the existing config-capture test that passes uvicorn_graceful_seconds=5 and asserts captured['kwargs']['timeout_graceful_shutdown'] == 5.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Rework the busy-gauge test so the uvicorn backstop actually bounds the exercised path, or remove the misleading uvicorn_backstop_seconds local and assertion and retitle to reflect what drain_then_exit verifies (gauge-driven drain vs certified-op grace).
evidence: tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_http_transport.py:658-665: drain_then_exit(...) is called with grace_seconds, poll_interval, sleep, monotonic, exit_fn — uvicorn_backstop_seconds is not among the arguments.

tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_http_transport.py:667: `assert uvicorn_backstop_seconds < now['t']` compares the literal 0.25 against fake elapsed time, not against any code-under-test behavior; drain_then_exit has no backstop parameter, so the uvicorn backstop is not exercised here at all.
advisory.finding: In test_mcp_retirement_busy_gauge_is_not_cut_short_by_uvicorn_backstop_40a7, the `uvicorn_backstop_seconds = 0.25` local is never passed into drain_then_exit and is unconnected to any uvicorn backstop; the assertion `uvicorn_backstop_seconds < now['t']` compares a bare literal against fake time and does not verify the stated 'not cut short by the uvicorn backstop' contract.
scenarios: The uvicorn backstop wiring truly truncated an in-flight op; this test would still pass because drain_then_exit never sees the backstop value.
